newsitem.title: GERMANY: Grundig says open to new partners.
newsitem.headline: Grundig says open to new partners.

text.p: German consumer electronics maker Grundig AG, set adrift by Dutch parent Philips AG, said on Wednesday it would seek new partners.
Grundig, which lost 250 million marks in 1996, scheduled a news conference for Friday where it would disclose further details.
"Grundig is opening itself to new partners, said chairman Pieter van der Wal in a statement.
"The Grundig board has introduced the needed steps to use the opportunities presented by the changing market for entertainment electronics together with strong partners," van der Wal said.
Philips said earlier it would scale back its role at Grundig to that of a passive minority shareholder.
Philips, which holds a 32 percent stake in Grundig, has managed the company under an agreement with the Max Grundig Foundation.
